overview: Markets: Wall Street fell and 30-year Treasury yields hit their highest since 2004 on Fed rate-hike bets, while Sensex and Nifty traded range-bound as the rupee hovered near 96/dollar on likely RBI intervention and IRDAI's commission-cap proposal wiped out a third of PB Fintech's value.

Big story: Presidents Trump and Xi Jinping held a high-stakes White House summit extending their trade truce while sparring over Taiwan, AI chips and Iran, even as US and Iranian negotiators explored a phased deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

items.headline: Trump and Xi extend trade truce at White House summit, spar over AI and Taiwan
items.summary: Presidents Trump and Xi Jinping met at the White House to discuss trade, AI safeguards, Taiwan and the Iran war, extending their fragile trade truce by two months after it had been set to expire in November. Xi wants a permanent halt to US arms sales to Taiwan and eased chip export curbs; Trump wants China's help pressuring Iran, underscoring how tech and security are now intertwined in great-power bargaining.

items.headline: Netanyahu defends Gaza and Iran campaigns in UN speech amid walkout
items.summary: Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu told the UN General Assembly Israel is fighting a 'seven-front war,' defended strikes on Iran as a matter of survival, and rejected genocide accusations over Gaza, prompting a delegate walkout. He also criticised the UK, Turkey, Qatar and New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, highlighting how isolated Israel's diplomatic position has become even among allies.

items.headline: US and Iran explore phased deal to reopen Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: US and Iranian negotiators are exploring a staged agreement in which Tehran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for Washington easing its blockade on Iranian ports, seven months into the 2026 Iran war. A breakthrough would ease record-high fuel prices and give both Trump and Iran's sanctions-hit economy relief, making it a pivotal swing factor for global oil markets and inflation.

items.headline: Pakistan strikes 10 Afghan locations in retaliation for Kohat mosque attack
items.summary: Pakistan carried out air and drone strikes on Taliban positions across Khost, Paktia, Paktika and Kandahar after drones launched from Afghanistan were shot down over Torkham and Kohat. The strikes follow a September 18 suicide bombing and gun attack on a mosque in Kohat that killed at least 31 people, marking a sharp escalation in the Pakistan-Afghanistan border conflict.

items.headline: Indian sailor killed as torpedoes hit merchant ship off Oman coast
items.summary: An Indian wiper, identified as Suraj Yadav from Uttar Pradesh, was killed when the Antigua-flagged MV Cape Dao was hit by two torpedoes near the Strait of Hormuz, sparking an engine-room fire. Oman's navy evacuated the rest of the crew; neither Iran nor the US has claimed responsibility, and at least 23 sailors have now died in Hormuz-area attacks since the Iran war began in February.

items.headline: Russian drone kills 14-year-old boy in Kyiv apartment strike
items.summary: A Russian drone slammed into a 16-storey residential building in Kyiv's Pecherskyi district, killing a 14-year-old boy and injuring at least seven people. President Zelensky mourned the death as Russia continues near-constant drone barrages on the capital that are increasingly hard for Ukrainian air defences to intercept.

items.headline: Pope Leo XIV begins first papal visit to France in nearly 20 years
items.summary: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Paris to open a four-day apostolic journey through France, starting with vespers at a restored Notre-Dame and a UNESCO address expected to touch on artificial intelligence. He will later meet clergy sex-abuse survivors in Lourdes, the first French papal trip since 2008.

items.headline: Belgium and Rwanda restore diplomatic ties after 18-month rupture
items.summary: Belgium and Rwanda agreed to resume diplomatic relations and reopen their embassies, ending a freeze that began in March 2025 over EU sanctions tied to Rwanda's alleged backing of M23 rebels in eastern Congo. Qatar helped broker the reconciliation, though both sides admit the underlying DRC dispute remains unresolved.

items.headline: Plea seeks CEC Gyanesh Kumar's prosecution over voter roll deletions
items.summary: A petition reached the Supreme Court seeking criminal prosecution of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over changes to Form 6 and a special voter registration drive that allegedly deleted or reprocessed over 13 crore names. The plea claims fellow commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected to at least 14 decisions taken without their concurrence, deepening a row over the Election Commission's independence ahead of state polls.

items.headline: IIT Bombay protests continue after student's suspected suicide
items.summary: Protests entered another day at IIT Bombay after 19-year-old Sahil Wakode's death by suicide in his hostel room, with Congress MP Varsha Gaikwad and NSUI activists detained outside campus. His parents have begun a hunger strike at Azad Maidan demanding an independent probe into alleged harassment and the institute's emergency response.

items.headline: Delhi's EV policy draws 5,678 applications, ₹4.8 crore disbursed
items.summary: Delhi's Electric Vehicle Policy 2026 has received 5,678 incentive applications since its July rollout, with 1,664 processed and ₹4.8 crore disbursed so far, mostly to two-wheeler buyers. The uptake signals steady momentum for the capital's EV push even as courts and civic agencies separately handle NIA-accused travel and gangrape-probe cases in the city.

items.headline: Mumbai deploys 24,000 police for Ganesh Visarjan on Anant Chaturdashi
items.summary: Mumbai and Maharashtra shut educational institutions as the city held its Ganesh Visarjan processions, with over 24,000 police personnel and 25,000 BMC staff deployed to manage crowds. The scale of the security operation underlines the civic and logistical load major Indian cities carry during large religious festivals.

items.headline: WEF survey names India world's strongest growth outlook for FY27
items.summary: In the World Economic Forum's September Chief Economists' Outlook, 74% of economists expect strong or very strong growth in India over the next year, up from 52% in May, with the FY27 forecast raised to 6.7%. Resilient domestic demand is cited as the driver, though economists flagged elevated energy prices as a risk, a reminder that India's growth story remains a key talking point in any macro or strategy interview.

items.headline: Sensex, Nifty trade flat-to-higher as FIIs sell, DIIs buy
items.summary: The Sensex opened lower near 73,525 before recovering to around 73,727 by midday, while the Nifty hovered near 23,035, dragged by IT stocks amid mixed global cues. Foreign investors sold ₹5,027 crore of equities on September 24 even as domestic institutions bought ₹4,301 crore, showing domestic flows continuing to cushion the market against FII outflows.

items.headline: Rupee holds near 96/dollar as RBI intervenes, October hike odds rise
items.summary: The rupee found temporary support near 96 to the dollar, with markets pointing to likely RBI intervention capping further declines even as US Treasury yields stayed elevated. August retail inflation rose to 4.8% year-on-year, its firmest since December 2024, increasing the odds of an RBI rate hike in October and squeezing the central bank's room to support growth.

items.headline: Wall Street slides as 30-year Treasury yield hits highest since 2004
items.summary: The S&P 500 closed down 0.75% at 7,706 and the Nasdaq fell over 1% as elevated oil prices stoked inflation worries and Fed rate-hike bets, sending the 30-year Treasury yield to its highest level since 2004 and the 10-year to 5.116%. The renewed bond volatility is spilling into emerging-market currencies, including the rupee, and raises the cost of capital globally just as companies plan next year's budgets.

items.headline: PB Fintech crashes 36% as IRDAI proposes insurance commission caps
items.summary: PB Fintech shares plunged 36%, wiping out roughly ₹25,000 crore ($3 billion) in market value, after IRDAI's consultation paper proposed capping insurer distribution costs at 15% of premium for life insurers within two years. Turtlemint hit its lower circuit and HDFC Life, ICICI Prudential Life and Max Financial also fell, illustrating how a single regulatory proposal can reprice an entire sector overnight.

items.headline: AceVector's IPO opens seeking valuation of up to ₹1,741 crore
items.summary: AceVector, the parent of Snapdeal, opened its IPO today with a price band of ₹30–32, comprising a ₹287 crore fresh issue and ₹133 crore offer for sale. The listing tests investor appetite for legacy e-commerce names even as India's primary market sees record retail participation, with over two dozen mainboard issues launched this month alone.

items.headline: AI industry leaders urge global regulation at UN Security Council
items.summary: Heads of major AI firms, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, told the UN Security Council their industry urgently needs global oversight to avoid dangers that could threaten humanity if AI development is mismanaged. The appeal reflects growing pressure on governments to coordinate AI safety rules even as the same companies race to commercialise ever more capable models.

items.headline: Amazon opens Seller Central to outside AI agents, starting with Claude
items.summary: At Amazon Accelerate, Amazon launched a US beta plugin letting third-party sellers manage inventory, pricing, listings and analytics through Anthropic's Claude or Amazon's own Quick assistant, running always-on agentic workflows without a seller logged in. Amazon says roughly 90% of sellers already use outside AI tools, signalling e-commerce platforms are ceding more operational control to AI agents.

items.headline: Anthropic says Claude discovered a novel CRISPR-like enzyme system
items.summary: Anthropic's new life sciences research group reported that Claude autonomously scanned roughly 1.9 billion protein clusters and identified a previously uncharacterised bacteriophage enzyme system, dubbed ART, whose repeat structure resembles CRISPR arrays. Around 950 AI agents ran for 21 hours using 210 million tokens to narrow 200,000 candidates down to 20 systems, though what ART actually does remains unknown.

items.headline: AI drone maker Tekever raises $580M, hits $6.4B valuation
items.summary: Portuguese-British defence startup Tekever raised the first close of a $580 million Series D led by UC Investments and Baillie Gifford, nearly quintupling its valuation to $6.4 billion. Its drones have logged over 50,000 flight hours supporting Ukraine, and it recently won a £400 million UK Ministry of Defence surveillance contract, underscoring surging investor appetite for European defence tech.

items.headline: West Indies tour of India begins Sunday with Gill, Jadeja back
items.summary: West Indies arrive for a three-ODI, five-T20I tour starting September 27 in Thiruvananthapuram, with Shubman Gill captaining the ODIs and Shreyas Iyer leading the T20Is. Ravindra Jadeja returns to the ODI squad after last playing in January, while Nitish Kumar Reddy has been pulled from the Asian Games squad to join the white-ball series.

items.headline: India win Asian Games shooting gold, hockey team beats Japan
items.summary: Suruchi Singh and Kamaljeet won gold in the mixed 10m air pistol event with an Asian-record 484.6 points, India's second gold at the 2026 Asian Games after the women's cricket team's win. India's women's hockey team also beat hosts Japan 3-1 to seal a semi-final berth, keeping their unbeaten run in Pool B intact.

items.headline: Laver Cup opens at London's O2 Arena with Alcaraz, Fritz in action
items.summary: The 2026 Laver Cup began at The O2 in London, with Team World defending its title after winning 15-9 in San Francisco last year. Carlos Alcaraz and Alexander Zverev lead Team Europe under captain Yannick Noah, while Taylor Fritz headlines Andre Agassi's Team World, as Formula 1 also races this weekend at the Baku Grand Prix in Azerbaijan.
